SPECIAL HANDLING
HI-SPECIFIC FORMS
If REPORTED time is listed, capture REPORTED time.
INCIDENT STATE
If blank, verify using the name of the police form. If it still cannot be determined, send to Bad Image.
REPORT TYPE
Report type is already extracted in Keying Form. As a keyer, verify if the extracted report type if matched with Image/Report's Report Type.
For mismatched report types:
Case 1: If keying form extracted as Auto Theft Recovery and report is Auto Theft, search for Recovery Date. If no recovery date is available, send to Bad Image with note "Missing Recovery Date/Details"
Case 2: If other mismatched report types cases, send to Bad Image with note "Mismatched Report Types: Keying Form extracted ___, report is ___."
For blank report types:
Verify using the Police form. If it still cannot be determined, send to Bad Image.
OTHER TERMS
Nature of Call • Incident Type • Incident Activities • Offenses • Vehicle Status/Code • Call Notes/Logs • Narrative
You can capture report type from narrative/call logs IF AND ONLY IF the report is a pure narrative or call logs.
See Report Type page for more information: Report Types
INCIDENT CITY, INCIDENT STREET, INCIDENT CROSS STREET
If missing, no need to send to bad image. Keyer may leave it blank.
OTHER TERMS
Address • Offense Location • Event Location • Incident Location • Recovery Address
INCIDENT CITY
Municipality, Town, and/or Village is keyable as Incident City.
DO NOT key County.
INCIDENT STREET/INCIDENT CROSS STREET
•There is only 1 incident street while incident cross street can have more than 1, except for forms like Arizona and Wyoming Standard Auto Accident form with specific field where KWYS rule is applied.
•Establishments are disregarded if address is also listed.
•For forms with two addresses are listed, usually separated by "/, "and", "@", in either of the Incident street or Incident Cross street and the other field is blank, keyer may separate and key the 1st address listed as Incident Street and 2nd address as Incident Cross Street. This doesn't apply to AZ and WY standard auto accident report.
AUTO THEFT RECOVERY
Case 1: If the report itself stated it is Auto Theft Recovery, capture Incident Address listed as Recovery Address.
Case 2: If keying form extracted as Auto Theft Recovery and report is Auto Theft, search for Recovery Address. If no recovery address is available, leave incident address blank.
LATITUDE/LONGITUDE
Degrees, minutes and seconds symbols(° ‘ ‘’) are disregarded and keyed without space.
Directions are only keyable if they are not pre-printed on the form as part of the standard layout.
Key coordinate X as Latitude and coordinate Y as Longitude.
OWNER DETAILS
MULTIPLE OWNER
For vehicles with more than 1 owner, key the 1st owner stated and disregard the other owner.
For forms with specific fields for owner and driver, if the report says the driver is also the owner, capture only the data needed for the owner
NAMING CONVENTIONS
Forms without naming format or no specified field for names, follow basic naming convention:
Case 1: First Name Middle Name Last Name Suffix
Case 2: Last Name Suffix, First Name Middle Name
Company Names is keyed as LAST NAME. If specific name fields/boxes are provided, still key as last name by following the FN MN LN SUFFIX arrangement.
For One Name listed, key as LN otherwise KWYS if listed on designated field.
ADDRESS 1 & 2
Directions and House Numbers are part of Address 1.
Lot, apartment, unit, room, suites, floor and such are considered as Address 2.
For reports where two City, State, and/or ZIP Code entries are provided in the Address field, key the 1st set of information as Address 2.
OUTSIDE US ADDRESS
If Address 1, Address 2, State, City and Zip is identifiable, key on its designated field. Otherwise, key the data in address 1.
PHONE NUMBER
Key What You See. Replace not keyable characters with space.
VIN
Replace letter "I" with "1", "O" & "Q" with "0"
VIN Decoder will then pop-up if VIN is valid. Check values from decoder if YEAR and MAKE match the report. Check which scenarios apply below:
If they match, click "OK" to accept the VIN. This will auto populate the YEAR, MAKE, and MODEL fields.
If they do not match, click "Cancel" and proceed to keying the YEAR, MAKE, and MODEL fields following KWYS.
If no Vehicle Year, Make and Model present in the report, accept the value provided by the VIN decoder.
AIRBAG
All occupants of a vehicle's airbag deployment should be considered.
If at least one has a deployed airbag, the Vehicle Airbag Deployment will be YES.
TEXT FIELD/FREEFORM FIELD
NULL VALUES
Unk • Unknown • UU • UK • N/A • Not Applicable • Not Available
These are only keyable in NAME FIELDS and CODED FIELDS(Fields with dropdown)
SERIES OF SAME NUMBER (ex. 000000000)

Follow KWYS rule.
CODED FIELDS
KWYS but make sure to check the codes and descriptions provided in the keying app. If there is a discrepancy, match descriptions and not the codes. At the same time, please report this to your supervisor or the TQA Team.
PARKED
If the status is PARKED and driver's name is also present, key the person indicated as driver still.
If no driver's name present, and there is an indicator/tick box indicating "parked", key PARKED in driver's last name field.
CONFLICTING/MISSING VEHICLE NUMBERS
If conflicting/missing vehicle numbers, we will still capture the data.
For reports where the vehicle number is absent, you can key the vehicles/parties in the order they are presented. Example, if you have 4 units listed, the first unit would be party 1, the second unit would be party 2, etc.
For reports where the agency gave two units the same unit number in error, you may use the narrative and diagram for clarification. NOTE: Any use of the narrative is strictly for clarification. Standard rules otherwise still apply as we would not use the narrative for any data mining.
For reports where there are multiples of one unit and there is a data conflict. For example, there are two drivers assigned to one unit. In this scenario, first check to see if the report has an amended version attached. If so, use the data associated with the amended version. If not, review the involved parties section for clarity if there is one. You may also review the narrative for clarification. If all options fail, you may key the parties as unknown. NOTE: If the there is a data conflict with the parties, but the vehicle information is normal, you must pick up the vehicle data.
For scenarios where there is one unit number and the other unit number is either blank or has a letter instead, please key the unit with the missing number. For example, if there is a report with a unit 1 and unit A, we would key unit A as vehicle 2.
VICTIM
Auto Accident
Victim is keyed as driver. If business/company, key as owner.
Auto Theft | Auto Theft Recovery | Auto Fire
It is considered as VEHICLE OWNER.
NOTE: If more than one victim and/or more than one vehicle, verify from narrative to assign them to the correct vehicle.
COMPLAINANT
Auto Accident

It should be keyed as UNKNOWN unless the report also stated a specified role for that person.
Auto Theft | Auto Theft Recovery | Auto Fire
It is considered as VEHICLE OWNER.
NOTE: For Auto Theft and Auto Theft Recovery, if Victim, Complainant and Reporting Party are all present, prioritize the Victim as Vehicle Owner.
REPORTING PARTY
Auto Accident

It should be keyed as UNKNOWN unless the report also stated a specified role for that person.
Auto Theft | Auto Theft Recovery | Auto Fire
It is considered as VEHICLE OWNER.
NOTE: For Auto Theft and Auto Theft Recovery, if Victim, Complainant and Reporting Party are all present, prioritize the Victim as Vehicle Owner.
SUSPECT/ARRESTEE/OFFENDER
Auto Accident
They should be keyed as driver.
Auto Theft | Auto Theft Recovery | Auto Fire
They are disregarded.

Keying Application Overview
The eCrash Keying Application is used for the purpose of keying data from police reports. From the Image Entry queue, if an image meets the minimum eligibility requirements for keying, the data will be extracted from the police report and keyed based on the general and state specific guidelines.
Once the image has been keyed, the data is saved, and the operator is presented with the next available report. The report is then available for keying by a second operator. Reports pass through two passes: 1st pass and 2nd pass entries. 3rd pass or additional keying will only be done per client request.
If there are no discrepancies between the data keyed by the 1st and 2nd Pass Operators, the VIN validation application will execute. This application is utilized to validate the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). If the VIN validates, the keying is complete, and no further handling is necessary.
If an operator is presented with an image that cannot be read, is missing pages or is ineligible for keying, the operator will send the image to the Bad Image Queue. Only operators with a super operator, supervisor or administrator operator role will be able to access this queue.

page_title: Keying Data from Reports: “Key What You See”
text:
Keying Data from Reports: “Key What You See”
When keying data from eligible reports, accuracy is imperative.
Data will be indexed for easy retrieval by insurance companies, law enforcement agencies and individual drivers. Data will also be aggregated as part of larger analysis tools. Incorrectly keyed data, in even a single field, can prevent an interested party from finding and purchasing a report. Additionally, these inaccuracies may mislead users causing an adverse impact on claim or other business decisions.
Data from an eligible report should be entered into the keying application as accurately as possible. The following rule is applicable in most circumstances: “Key What You See.”
For each state, the default report template utilized in the keying application is the state’s standard form. The standard form has been selected as the default report template as most law enforcement agencies within the same state will use either the same report or a similar version. Reports not written on the standard form is called a nonstandard form and should still be keyed if they meet the minimum eligibility requirements. It is the operator’s responsibility to ensure that the correct data is taken from the police report and entered into the correct fields within the keying application. Any exceptions to the “Key What You See” rule will be covered in the state specific rules as warranted.

The Four Required Fields
In addition to the report classification a report must have the following two data elements before it can be considered eligible for keying.
Date of Loss (Incident Date)
Frequent terminology used for Date of loss
– Accident Date
– Crash Date
– Date of Crash
– Investigation Date
– Occurred On
– Reported On
Report Number (Report Identifier #1)

Ø Report Identifier # 2
Some agencies will have two report identifiers on a standard crash report. The state report number is for the state record. If a state report number is available, please capture that information in the Report Identifier # 2 field. Frequent terminology used for state numbers are:
TXDOT Crash ID
Official DMV Use
REPORT NO.

Incident State
Report Type
See GENERAL SOP page for more information.

Report Types
A= Auto Accident
An auto accident involves at least one road vehicle. Examples of road vehicles include, but are not limited to the following; Cars, Trucks, Semi-trucks, Recreational vehicles (R.Vs), Buses, Motorcycles, Mopeds, Bicycles, All terrain vehicles (ATVs), Golf carts etc.
The following are not deemed as motor vehicles.
Ø Farm equipment (tractors, balers, etc.)
Ø Bulldozers
Ø Airplanes or helicopters
Ø Construction equipment
Ø Watercraft (motorboats, sailboats, houseboats, or jet skis)
Ø Flatbed trailers
B= Auto Theft
An auto theft involves a stolen vehicle or boat. We will key these reports as long as theft was completed (not attempted).
C= Auto Theft Recovery
An auto theft recovery occurs when a vehicle or boat was recovered from being stolen
F= Auto Fire
An auto/car fire is when a road or boat was on fire. Building fires that involves vehicles is also a valid document.
Any report involving vandalism, vehicle parts stolen, arson, robbery, burglary, arrest reports, criminal reports will be discarded into Bad Image.

page_title: Words, Abbreviations and/or Characters Representing Null
text:
Words, Abbreviations and/or Characters Representing Null
When completing reports, officers frequently use words, abbreviations, or characters to represent null values. As these words/abbreviations/characters act only as place holders, they are ineligible for keying. The field should remain blank in the keying application.
Below is a list of commonly used words, abbreviations and/or characters used to represent null values.
Examples
Unknown
Not Available
Unknown
NA
UNK
N/A
UK
UU
Note: The abbreviations and characters listed in the chart are ineligible for keying as they represent data that is missing, unavailable or unknown. However, if an officer uses terminology such as “No Insurance” in the insurance field, the data would be eligible for keying. “No Insurance” is a known value. At the time of the accident, the driver did not have insurance. Also, when the value of “UNK or UNKNOWN” is presented on a report in the name fields; the keyers are to Key What You See (KWYS).
See GENERAL SOP page for more information.

Reviewing and Keying Non-standard Forms
Many law enforcement agencies utilize Computer-assisted Dispatch, also called Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD), to manage dispatch activities more efficiently. CAD typically consists of a suite of software packages used for initiating and monitoring call input, call dispatching, call status and maintenance, event notes, field unit status and tracking, and call resolution and disposition.
A report generated from CAD may or may not be referred to as a “CAD Report.” For example, only one includes the acronym “CAD” in the report title; however, all three reports are versions of a CAD report.
Depending on the type of accident/incident that prompted the law enforcement response, the CAD report may be used in conjunction with a standard form, or it may be the only report generated by the agency.
If these reports are received, it is important to quickly check thru/browse the entire document to determine if a standard form is attached.
If a report has both Standard form and non-standard form, you pull information from both and for any conflicts, normal keying rules apply
If a standard form is not received, the document should be reviewed to determine if it meets the minimum eligibility requirements for keying. The report must have a date of loss and report number, and it should be classified as an auto accident, auto theft, auto theft recovery, or auto fire. To determine the report’s classification, the operator should scan the document for any keywords indicating that it does not pertain to an ineligible incident/report. Keywords include, but are not limited to, burglary, theft, fire, etc.
If the report is deemed eligible for keying, the data should be entered into the appropriate fields within the keying application. Please see the state guides for state specific rules and helpful hints for common CAD reports.
Frequently used terminology for nonstandard forms
Investigative Reports
Incident Report
Police Report
Call History Record
General Offense Records
CAD Call
Driver Information Exchange
Officer Report for Incident
Accident Report

Tips in Keying Data Elements
Date of Birth Field
The Date of Birth (DOB) field in the keying application is formatted as MM/DD/YYYY. Once the field is selected, the slashes are automatically populated. A DOB must be entered as 8 numbers. If the DOB is listed in a different format on an eligible report, it is permissible to correct the format to insure it is entered correctly into the keying application. For example, if the Driver’s DOB is listed as “February 18, 1964” or “18 February 1964” on the report, the DOB should be keyed as follows: 02/18/1964.
If the DOB has been partially redacted (removed), no data should be keyed and this field should be skipped. The field will not accept invalid months, days or years. For example, a zero cannot be utilized as a placeholder for a redacted portion of a DOB.
If the DOB is incorrect, still key what you see.
If the DOB is missing the year leave DOB field blank.
Name Fields
When entering names into the keying application, the order and format is extremely important. Names should be entered in the following format: first name, middle name, last name and suffix. The name fields within the keying application, with a few exceptions, consist of four boxes: First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, and the suffix. If the name is recorded on the report as “John E. Doe,” the name would be keyed into the boxes as shown below.
First Name
Middle Name
Last Name
John
E
Doe
Commas in Names
Aside from removing non-alphanumeric (except hyphenated names) data and special characters from text fields, it is important to “Key What You See.” Do not make assumptions about the order of names. It can be difficult to differentiate a first name from a last name, so it is important to key the names in the order recorded by the Officer. The Officer will usually follow the format prescribed on the report form.
However, if the name is recorded with a comma, it is permissible to change the order of names. A comma is used when the format of a name is recorded as follows: Last Name, First Name, and Middle Initial. If a comma is used, it can be safely assumed that the name listed first is the last name followed by the first and middle. For example, if the name is recorded as “Doe, John E,” the name would be keyed into the boxes as shown below.
First Name
Middle Name
Last Name
John
E
Doe
Business Names
When business name is given key this information in the last name field.
If the business name is recorded with a comma, it is permissible to change the order of the name.
For example.
INC, GEIGO
GEICO INC
Suffixes
The fourth box in the name field is used to record suffixes. A suffix is used after a person’s full name and provides additional information about the person.
Generational titles are an example of a suffix. These specific suffixes are used to distinguish persons who would otherwise share the same name within a family. The most used generational suffixes are Junior (Jr.), Senior (Sr.), and Roman Numerals (II, II, etc).
Post-nominal letters, while less common on police reports, may also be encountered. These letters indicate that an individual holds a position, educational degree, accreditation, office or honor. Common examples are Esq., RN, USMC, Ph.D, M.D.
Policy Numbers
If the officer recorded two insurance policy numbers, both numbers should be keyed and a comma should be used to separate the two. All other scenarios, key what you see.
Incident Street/Cross Street
Please key the incident street/cross street that is listed on the report even if it was not at an Intersection’.
Using example 1 below, the yellow highlighted text below (and ONLY the yellow highlighted text) would be keyed into Incident Street and Incident Cross Street fields in Keying App.
We will not be keying the extra elements that go along with the second street (ie. ‘feet/miles’, ‘location S/SW/N/NW unless it is stated in the state specific requirement section.)
